newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia money rates steady before reserve payment.
newsitem.headline: Croatia money rates steady before reserve payment.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates held steady in moderate activity on Monday ahead of the reserve payment, dealers said.
But the central bank said it gave three banks some 60 million kuna in Lombard loans this morning to bail them out of a temporary liquidity crisis.
Lombard loans are granted at 9.5 percent for a maximum of 12 working days a month.
By 1130 local (0930 GMT), the money market trade reached a modest 22.5 million kuna, with another three million in demand that creditors refused to grant despite enough funds on supply.
Some banks were also repaying previous borrowings, but that did not disturb the market, one dealer told Reuters.
All new call money deals were struck at a flat 10.5 percent.
One-week to one-month rates ranged between 12 and 15 percent, also unchanged from recent levels.
Dealers put the weekend overnight trade at 50 million kuna as one bank borrowed money to square its sizeable shortfall and another to maintain statutory reserves.
The banking sector ended last week with a total balance of 453 million kuna.
